title: Nvidia Board Opens Probe After CEO Jensen Huang Admits to Affair Amid Chinese Spy Allegations
snippet: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an extramarital affair, prompting an independent board investigation following reports connecting his personal relationship to alleged Chinese intelligence activities.
content:
Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang acknowledged Sunday that he engaged in an extramarital affair, prompting an independent board inquiry following reports alleging his partner was an intelligence asset for the Chinese government.

In a internal memo addressed to employees, Huang expressed deep remorse for his conduct, apologizing to his family, workforce, and global investors. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Huang wrote. He added that he remains "fully committed to Nvidia" and intends to work to regain stakeholder confidence.

Board Initiates Independent Review

Nvidia's board of directors confirmed Sunday that a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside legal counsel, will oversee a thorough inquiry into the situation. The action follows recent reporting from The New York Times indicating US intelligence officials suspected Alice Huang—a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed with documented ties to the CEO—of passing information to Beijing.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board stated.

Scrutiny from Wall Street and Washington

The fallout arrives at a sensitive time for the Silicon Valley semiconductor giant, which has faced mounting pressure over US export restrictions banning the sale of advanced AI chips to China.

Financial analysts noted that the probe introduces corporate governance risks and potential regulatory scrutiny in Washington. Wedbush analyst Dan Ives described the development as a "black eye" for Huang that could spark congressional inquiries. While Ives expects Huang to remain CEO during the near term, he cautioned that any shift in leadership could weigh on the stock, given Huang's key role in guiding Nvidia's dominant position in the global artificial intelligence boom.
